questions: Did line_loss_events fall below 1 on the s-bend and slalom with the shorter, lighter, narrower-track body?
Did max_error drop below 0.06 on any track, and at what progress does the robot leave the track now?
Did steering_oscillation rise with the higher turn rate from the narrower track? If it did, the turn gain is too high for the controller.
If the robot holds the line, is completion_time above 3.0 s, and does that point to speed (wheel_radius) rather than turning?

intent: Test whether turning authority and yaw inertia, not sensor coverage, limit line following. Keep the iteration 2 sensor array unchanged, then reduce mass to 0.5 kg, body_length to 0.12 m and wheel_track to 0.10 m. The body is shorter, so yaw inertia falls by about half, and the narrower track raises turn rate for the same PWM difference. Expected result: line_loss_events below 1 and max_error below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom, with progress rising above 0.15. If the robot stays on the line but still exceeds 3.0 s, the next change is to raise wheel_radius to 0.035 m.
learning: Sensor span, footprint and lead have each been tested with almost no change in max_error, so I am moving to the drivetrain. If turning authority is the limit, this change should show a clear drop in line loss and max_error. If it has no effect, the limit is elsewhere (likely speed or sensor response), and I will revisit the footprint at 0.012 m and a larger wheel radius next. The Integrator should report whether the higher turn rate causes oscillation, since that would mean the controller needs lower gains rather than more geometry change.
rationale: Iteration 2 (lead moved to y = 0.04 m) scored 50.07, slightly below iteration 1 (50.13). Line_loss_events stayed at 1 on the oval, s-bend and slalom, and max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.069. Progress is still only 0.10 to 0.15 and oscillation is low. Across three iterations, the sensor span (±0.02 to ±0.03 m), the footprint (12 to 16 mm) and the lead (0.05 to 0.04 m) have each changed max_error by less than 0.001 m. The sensor array is therefore not the binding limit. The robot is leaving the tape with a steady drift rather than oscillating, which suggests the body cannot turn quickly enough for the bends at its current speed. Two geometry levers affect turning directly. Yaw inertia is mass*(body_length²+body_width²)/12, so a shorter body and lighter mass reduce the inertia the wheels must overcome. Turn rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more turn rate per unit of PWM difference. This iteration keeps the sensor array from iteration 2 exactly, so the score change can be attributed to the drivetrain and body. I reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg, shorten body_length from 0.18 to 0.12 m, and narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. I expect line_loss_events to fall below 1 on the bends and max_error to drop below 0.06 on at least the s-bend and slalom. The completion_time question stays open until the robot holds the line.
